summary:
Land, Mathew, Meier and Tamme prove a purity theorem for chromatically localized algebraic K-theory. For a ring spectrum — an E_1-algebra in spectra — and an integer n ≥ 1, the canonical map A → L_{T(n−1)⊕T(n)}A induces an equivalence on T(n)-local K-theory: the T(n)-local K-theory of A depends only on the two adjacent chromatic layers n−1 and n of A. The theorem has two halves. The half proved here is Theorem A: A → L_{T(0)⊕⋯⊕T(n)}A is an equivalence on L_{T(n)}K(−) for n ≥ 1, and A → L_{T(1)⊕⋯⊕T(n)}A is one for n ≥ 2. The other half is Clausen–Mathew–Naumann–Noel's vanishing of L_{T(n)}K(L_{n−2}^{p,f}S), whose proof uses Theorem A but not the Purity Theorem, so the two fit together without circularity.

The proof runs in three steps. First, using the plus-construction description of connective K-theory, the Bousfield–Kuhn functor and Bousfield's vanishing theorem for v_i-periodic homotopy, a sufficiently connective L_n^{p,f}-equivalence of connective ring spectra induces an L_n^{p,f}-equivalence on K-theory. Second, this is upgraded through the Land–Tamme pullback theorem to the statement that L_{T(n)}K(−) is truncating on L_n^{p,f}-acyclic ring spectra. Third, the S_•-construction and the Thomason–Neeman localization sequence 𝒞_{>n} ⊗ Perf(A) → Perf(A) → Perf(L_n^{p,f}A) reduce the general case to the connective one; Mitchell's theorem that K(Z) has no telescopic homotopy above height one supplies the base of the induction. Ishan Levy's Proposition 3.12 gives a second proof of the key vanishing through a stable category with a bounded t-structure and the theorem of the heart.

The consequences occupy §4. Theorem B is the redshift inequality hgt(K(R)) ≤ hgt(R)+1 for an E_∞-ring, which with Yuan's and Burklund–Schlank–Yuan's converse gives the Redshift Theorem. K(K(n)) vanishes T(m)-locally for m ≠ 0, n, n+1; K(BP⟨n⟩) → K(E(n)) is a T(i)-equivalence for i ≥ n+1; L_{T(i)}K(τ_{≤n}S) = 0 for i ≥ 2, which settles a conjecture of Antieau; K(y(m)) and K(z(m)) vanish telescopically below height m. For ko-algebras and tmf-algebras inverting the Bott element or the discriminant is invisible to telescopic K-theory, and at the prime 2 one gets L_{T(3)}K(tmf) ≃ K(E_2)^{hGL_2(F_3)}. At height one, K(1)-local K-theory is truncating on K(1)-acyclic ring spectra and therefore nilinvariant, homotopy invariant, and satisfies Milnor excision and cdh-descent. At heights n ≥ 2, K, the connective cover and TC all agree telescopically, group-completion K-theory suffices in place of Waldhausen K-theory, and the Farrell–Jones assembly map for the family of cyclic subgroups is a T(n)-equivalence.

What the paper needs is chromatic homotopy theory — type n complexes and v_n self-maps, Morava K-theories, telescopes, Bousfield classes, the finite localizations L_n^f and L_n^{p,f}, the Bousfield–Kuhn functor, Hahn's theorem, Kuhn's blueshift, ko, tmf and Lubin–Tate theory — none of which the atlas has anywhere, together with algebraic K-theory of stable ∞-categories and ring spectra, which GeneralAlgebraicKTheory and RefinedTraceMethods own in their classical forms.

items.name: Conventions: spectra, ring spectra and modules
items.statement: A prime p is fixed and is the implicit prime of all Morava K-theories K(i) and telescopes T(i); K(0) = HQ. A ring spectrum means an E_1-ring, that is an algebra in the symmetric monoidal ∞-category Sp of spectra, and a module means a right module; for an E_k-ring R with k ≥ 2, an R-algebra is an algebra in RMod(R). For a spectrum X and a pointed space Y, X ⊗ Y denotes the smash product X ⊗ Σ^∞Y.
items.locator: §1, Conventions, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043
items.note: H.5:spectra plans a concrete model of spectra with suspension spectra, loops and shift, integer-indexed stable homotopy groups, fibres and cofibres; E5:abstract plans symmetric monoidal ∞-categories with their operadic algebras and modules, which is what an E_k-ring and its module and algebra categories are; E5:presentability plans Ind-completion and compact objects. Nothing in the atlas fixes the smash product of a spectrum with a pointed space, but that is a definition rather than a target.

items.name: Bousfield localization at a spectrum
items.statement: For a spectrum E, a spectrum X is E-acyclic if E ⊗ X = 0 and E-local if it receives no nonzero maps from E-acyclic spectra; a map is an E-equivalence if its fibre is E-acyclic. The Bousfield localization L_E is the reflection of Sp onto the E-local spectra, and the Bousfield class of E is its class of acyclics, so that L_E depends only on the Bousfield class. L_E is smashing if it preserves colimits, equivalently if L_EX ≃ X ⊗ L_ES, and finite if every E-acyclic spectrum is a filtered colimit of compact E-acyclic spectra; every finite localization is smashing.
items.locator: §1 Conventions and §2.2, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Bousfield, The localization of spectra with respect to homology, Topology 18 (1979), 257–281)

items.name: Theorem A: the two halves of purity
items.statement: Theorem A. Let A be a ring spectrum. (i) For n ≥ 1 the canonical map A → L_{T(0)⊕⋯⊕T(n)}A induces an equivalence on T(n)-local K-theory. (ii) For n ≥ 2 the canonical map A → L_{T(1)⊕⋯⊕T(n)}A induces an equivalence on T(n)-local K-theory.
items.locator: Theorem A (§1), restated and proved as Theorem 3.8, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (Clausen–Mathew–Naumann–Noel): vanishing of K(L_{n-2}^{p,f}S)
items.statement: Theorem 1.1. For n ≥ 2, the K-theory of L_{T(0)⊕⋯⊕T(n−2)}S vanishes T(n)-locally. It is a special case of Theorem C of Clausen–Mathew–Naumann–Noel, whose proof uses Theorem A but not the Purity Theorem, so there is no circularity.
items.locator: Theorem 1.1, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Clausen–Mathew–Naumann–Noel, Descent and vanishing in chromatic algebraic K-theory via group actions, Ann. Sci. Éc. Norm. Supér. 57 (2024), 1135–1190, Theorem C)

items.name: The Purity Theorem
items.statement: Purity Theorem. Let A be a ring spectrum. For n ≥ 1 the canonical map A → L_{T(n−1)⊕T(n)}A induces an equivalence in T(n)-local K-theory. It follows from Theorem A and Theorem 1.1 by a fracture-square argument, and it is optimal: A ↦ L_{T(n)}K(A) factors through neither A ↦ L_{T(n−1)}A nor A ↦ L_{T(n)}A.
items.locator: The Purity Theorem (§1), proved in §3.3, with optimality in Remark 3.11, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: The height of an E_∞-ring, after Hahn
items.statement: Hahn proved that for any n a T(n)-acyclic E_∞-ring is also T(n+1)-acyclic; one therefore defines the height of an E_∞-ring R as hgt(R) = inf{n ≥ −1 : R ⊗ T(n+1) = 0}. Redshift in this language is the statement hgt(K(R)) = hgt(R) + 1 for E_∞-rings of non-negative height; the restriction to non-negative height is necessary, since hgt(K(F_p^{tC_p})) = −1 ≠ hgt(F_p^{tC_p}) + 1.
items.locator: §1 (Redshift) with its footnote, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Hahn, On the Bousfield classes of H_∞-rings)

items.name: Theorem B: the redshift inequality
items.statement: Theorem B. For an E_∞-ring R, hgt(K(R)) ≤ hgt(R) + 1. It is an immediate consequence of the Purity Theorem and is also Theorem A of Clausen–Mathew–Naumann–Noel.
items.locator: Theorem B (§1), Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: The Redshift Theorem
items.statement: Redshift Theorem (Yuan; Burklund–Schlank–Yuan; Theorem B). For an E_∞-ring R with hgt(R) ≥ 0, hgt(K(R)) = hgt(R) + 1. The converse inequality is due to Yuan, who proved hgt(K(E_n)) ≥ hgt(E_n)+1 for Lubin–Tate theory E_n using Theorem A and a T-equivariant Dennis trace argument reducing to hgt(K((τ_{≥0}E_n)^{tC_p})) ≥ n, and to Burklund–Schlank–Yuan, whose chromatic Nullstellensatz gives, for n ≥ 0 and any E_∞-ring R with L_{T(n)}R ≠ 0, an E_∞-map R → E_n for a suitable (𝔾,k).
items.locator: Redshift Theorem (§1), Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Yuan, Examples of chromatic redshift in algebraic K-theory, Theorem A; Burklund–Schlank–Yuan, The Chromatic Nullstellensatz, Theorem D)

items.name: Redshift as a statement about graded pieces of the chromatic filtration
items.statement: By Lemma 2.3, for a ring spectrum the nth graded piece of the telescopic filtration {L_n^{p,f}X} vanishes if and only if the nth graded piece of the chromatic filtration {L_n^pX} does. The Redshift Theorem therefore says: for an E_∞-ring R with hgt(R) ≥ 0, the nth graded piece of the chromatic filtration of R is trivial if and only if the (n+1)st graded piece of the chromatic filtration of K(R) is.
items.locator: §1 (Redshift), final paragraph, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary C: inverting p for T(1)-acyclic ring spectra
items.statement: Corollary C. For a T(1)-acyclic ring spectrum A, the canonical map K(A) → K(A[1/p]) is a T(1)-local equivalence. This recovers, by purely homotopy-theoretic and K-theoretic methods, the theorem of Bhatt–Clausen–Mathew for HZ-algebras that a T(0)-equivalence of HZ-algebras induces an equivalence on T(1)-local K-theory.
items.locator: Corollary C (§1), proved as Corollary 4.23, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Bhatt–Clausen–Mathew, Remarks on K(1)-local K-theory)

items.name: Corollary D: K of Morava K-theory and of BP⟨n⟩
items.statement: Corollary D. (i) For positive integers m ≠ n, n+1 the spectrum K(K(n)) is T(m)-acyclic. (ii) The map K(BP⟨n⟩) → K(E(n)) is a T(m)-equivalence for m ≥ n+1, and both terms vanish T(m)-locally for m ≥ n+2.
items.locator: Corollary D (§1), proved as Corollaries 4.9 and 4.12, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary E: connective cover and cyclotomic trace at heights ≥ 2
items.statement: Corollary E. Let A be a ring spectrum. For n ≥ 2 the maps K(A) ← K(τ_{≥0}A) → TC(τ_{≥0}A), induced by the connective cover and the cyclotomic trace, are T(n)-local equivalences.
items.locator: Corollary E (§1), proved as Corollary 4.30, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary F: the cyclic-subgroup assembly map at heights ≥ 2
items.statement: Corollary F. For a ring spectrum A, a group G and n ≥ 2, the assembly map colim_{G/H ∈ 𝒪_𝒞(G)} K(AH) → K(AG) over the orbit category of G for the family of cyclic subgroups is a T(n)-local equivalence, where AG = A ⊗ Σ^∞_+G.
items.locator: Corollary F (§1), proved as Corollary 4.34, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Type n complexes, v_n self-maps and the periodicity theorem
items.statement: For n ≥ 1, V_n denotes a type n complex — a pointed finite CW complex with K(i) ⊗ V_n = 0 for i < n and K(n) ⊗ V_n ≠ 0 — and v_n a v_n self-map, that is a map Σ^dV_n → V_n for some d > 0 inducing an isomorphism on K(n)-homology and nilpotent maps on K(i)-homology for i ≠ n. Such maps exist by the periodicity theorem of Hopkins and Smith.
items.locator: §2.1, first paragraph, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Hopkins–Smith, Nilpotence and stable homotopy theory II, Ann. of Math. 148 (1998))

items.name: v_n-periodic homotopy groups and v_n-periodic equivalences
items.statement: For a pointed space or spectrum X, v_n^{−1}π_*(X;V_n) := Z[v_n^{±1}] ⊗_{Z[v_n]} π_*Map_*(V_n,X). Definition 2.1: a map is a v_n-periodic equivalence (n ≥ 1) if it induces an isomorphism on these groups; a map of spectra or simple spaces is a v_0-periodic equivalence if it becomes an equivalence after inverting p, the v_0-periodic homotopy groups being the homotopy groups with p inverted. A spectrum X is E-acyclic if E ⊗ X = 0, and a map is an E-equivalence if its fibre is E-acyclic.
items.locator: §2.1 with Definition 2.1, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Telescopes T(n) and Bousfield classes
items.statement: For a fixed pair (V_n,v_n), T(n) := Σ^∞V_n[v_n^{−1}] is the telescope of v_n, with the convention T(0) = S[1/p]. The Bousfield class of a spectrum E is the full subcategory of Sp of E-acyclic spectra. L_{T(n)} is called telescopic localization at height n and the implicit prime p; for n = 1 it agrees with L_{K(1)} by theorems of Miller and Mahowald.
items.locator: §2.1, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Lemma 2.2: basic properties of telescopic localization
items.statement: Lemma 2.2. For a spectrum X and a pointed space Y: (i) v_n^{−1}π_*(X;V_n) ≅ v_n^{−1}π_*(Ω^∞X;V_n); (ii) τ_{≥k}X → X and τ_{≥k}Y → Y are v_n-periodic equivalences for all k and all n ≥ 1; (iii) K(m) is T(n)-acyclic for n ≠ m; (iv) any T(n)-acyclic spectrum is K(n)-acyclic; (v) an S/p-acyclic spectrum is T(n)-acyclic for all n ≥ 1; (vi) X → X^∧_p is a T(n)-equivalence for all n ≥ 1; (vii) the Bousfield class of T(n) does not depend on the choice of (V_n,v_n); (viii) a spectrum is T(n)-acyclic if and only if its v_n-periodic homotopy groups vanish.
items.locator: Lemma 2.2, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: The status of the telescope conjecture
items.statement: The converse of Lemma 2.2(iv) for n ≥ 1 is the telescope conjecture. It is true in height 1 by Mahowald and Miller, and was recently disproved at all higher heights and all primes by Burklund–Hahn–Levy–Schlank.
items.locator: §2.1, the remark after Lemma 2.2, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Mahowald; Miller; Burklund–Hahn–Levy–Schlank, K-theoretic counterexamples to Ravenel's telescope conjecture)

items.name: Lemma 2.3: the telescope conjecture holds for ring spectra
items.statement: Lemma 2.3. Let R be a ring spectrum and n ≥ 1. Then R is K(n)-acyclic if and only if it is T(n)-acyclic. The proof is a consequence of the nilpotence theorem, and Remark 2.4 notes that it does not use that R is an algebra in Sp: it suffices that R be a unital magma in the homotopy category of spectra.
items.locator: Lemma 2.3 with Remark 2.4, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: The localizations L_n^f and L_n^{p,f}
items.statement: L_n^f is the Bousfield localization at HQ ⊕ T(1) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ T(n). Definition 2.5: L_n^{p,f} is the Bousfield localization at T(0) ⊕ T(1) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ T(n). A Bousfield localization L is smashing if it preserves colimits, equivalently if LX ≃ X ⊗ LS, and finite if every L-acyclic spectrum is a colimit of compact L-acyclic spectra; a finite localization is smashing.
items.locator: §2.2 with Definition 2.5, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Lemma 2.6: L_n^{p,f} is a finite, hence smashing, localization
items.statement: Lemma 2.6. Writing 𝒞_{>n} for the ∞-category of p-local finite spectra of type greater than n, that is those which are K(0) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ K(n)-acyclic, the category of L_n^{p,f}-acyclic spectra coincides with Ind(𝒞_{>n}); in particular L_n^{p,f} is a smashing localization.
items.locator: Lemma 2.6, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Lemma 2.7: the chromatic fracture square for L_n^{p,f}
items.statement: Lemma 2.7. For integers 0 ≤ m < n and a spectrum X there is a pullback square, natural in X, with corners L_n^{p,f}X, L_{T(m+1)⊕⋯⊕T(n)}X, L_m^{p,f}X and L_m^{p,f}L_{T(m+1)⊕⋯⊕T(n)}X.
items.locator: Lemma 2.7, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Lemma 2.8: a fracture square for a sum of two localizations
items.statement: Lemma 2.8. Let E and F be spectra and assume that L_E preserves F-acyclic spectra. Then there is a pullback square, natural in X, with corners L_{E⊕F}X, L_FX, L_EX and L_EL_FX. The assumption holds for instance if L_E is smashing, or if L_F annihilates E-local objects.
items.locator: Lemma 2.8 with the sentence after it, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Two consequences of Lemma 2.8
items.statement: For p-local spectra X the canonical map L_n^{p,f}X → L_n^fX is an equivalence, and for T(1)-acyclic spectra X the canonical map L_1^{p,f}X → X[1/p] is an equivalence.
items.locator: §2.2, the two displayed consequences of Lemma 2.8, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Proposition 2.9: Σ^∞Ω^∞ detects T(i)-local equivalences
items.statement: Proposition 2.9. Let f : X → Y be a map of spectra and i ≥ 1. If Σ^∞Ω^∞f is a T(i)-local equivalence then so is f; that is, Σ^∞Ω^∞ : Sp → Sp detects T(i)-local equivalences. Remark 2.10 adds that, restricted to connective spectra, it also detects T(0)-local equivalences. It does not, however, preserve T(i)-local equivalences: HZ is T(i)-acyclic whereas Σ^∞Z is not, containing the sphere as a summand.
items.locator: Proposition 2.9 with Remark 2.10 and the paragraph after it, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Proposition 2.11: Σ^∞Ω^∞ preserves highly connective L_n^{p,f}-equivalences
items.statement: Proposition 2.11. For n ≥ 1 there exists m ≥ 2 such that: (i) an m-connective pointed space F whose v_i-periodic homotopy groups vanish for 0 ≤ i ≤ n is T(i)-acyclic for 0 ≤ i ≤ n; (ii) an m-connective map f : X → Y of spaces which is a v_i-periodic equivalence for 0 ≤ i ≤ n at every basepoint has Σ^∞f an L_n^{p,f}-equivalence at every basepoint; (iii) Σ^∞Ω^∞ preserves m-connective L_n^{p,f}-equivalences. Here a space is m-connective if it has trivial homotopy in degrees < m, and a map is m-connective if the fibre over every basepoint is.
items.locator: Proposition 2.11 with the definitions preceding it, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Remark 2.12: one may take m = n+1
items.statement: Remark 2.12. In fact m = n+1 works in Proposition 2.11. It suffices that an (n+1)-connective space F with p-primary torsion homotopy vanishing in high degrees be T(i)-acyclic for 0 ≤ i ≤ n, and by induction over the Postnikov tower it suffices that T(i) ⊗ K(π,r) = 0 for r > i and π finite. Carmeli–Schlank–Yanovski show that for a p-local ring spectrum R the conditions R ⊗ K(π,r) = 0 for all r > i and R ⊗ K(r) = 0 for all r > i are equivalent; the second holds for R = T(i) by Lemma 2.2(iii). This remark is not used in the sequel.
items.locator: Remark 2.12, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Carmeli–Schlank–Yanovski, Ambidexterity and height, Theorem E)

items.name: Localizing invariants, Cat_∞^perf and K-theory of ring spectra
items.statement: A localizing invariant is a functor Cat_∞^perf → Sp sending exact sequences to fibre sequences, where Cat_∞^perf is the ∞-category of small, idempotent complete, stable ∞-categories and exact sequences are those which are both fibre and cofibre sequences there. Non-connective K-theory, THH and TC are localizing invariants. For a localizing invariant E and a ring spectrum A one writes E(A) for E(Perf(A)), where Perf(A) — the compact objects of RMod(A) — is the ∞-category of perfect A-modules.
items.locator: §2.3, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Blumberg–Gepner–Tabuada, A universal characterization of higher algebraic K-theory, §§5, 9)

items.name: The plus-construction description of connective K-theory
items.statement: For a connective ring spectrum A, Ω^∞τ_{≥1}K(A) is the plus construction BGL(A)^+, where GL(A) = colim GL_n(A) and GL_n(A) is the invertible components of the E_1-space Ω^∞End(A^n), so that π_0GL(A) ≅ GL(π_0A). In particular BGL(A) → Ω^∞τ_{≥1}K(A) is a homology equivalence and Σ^∞BGL(A) → Σ^∞Ω^∞τ_{≥1}K(A) is an equivalence of spectra.
items.locator: §2.3, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Blumberg–Gepner–Tabuada, Lemma 9.39)

items.name: The S_•-construction and its delooping
items.statement: For 𝒞 ∈ Cat_∞^perf, Waldhausen's S_•-construction gives a simplicial object S_•𝒞 ∈ Fun(Δ^op, Cat_∞^perf) with a natural equivalence of spaces Ω^∞K(𝒞) ≃ Ω|S_•(𝒞)^≃|, where (−)^≃ is the underlying space, and S_n(𝒞) ≃ Fun(Δ^{n−1},𝒞) for each n ≥ 0. Both sides are E_∞-spaces because Cat_∞^perf is semiadditive, the equivalence is one of E_∞-spaces, and delooping gives Ω^∞(τ_{≥0}K(𝒞)[1]) ≃ |S_•(𝒞)^≃|.

Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Blumberg–Gepner–Tabuada §7.1; Gepner–Groth–Nikolaus, Definition 2.1)

items.name: Proposition 3.1: the highly connective case
items.statement: Proposition 3.1. Let n ≥ 1. There exists N ≥ 1 such that the following holds: if A → B is an N-connective L_n^{p,f}-equivalence between connective ring spectra, then K(A) → K(B) is again an L_n^{p,f}-equivalence. One may take N = m−1 for the m of Proposition 2.11. The proof passes to BGL through the plus-construction description, uses that B raises connectivity by one and preserves v_i-periodic equivalences, that τ_{≥1}GL(A) ≃ τ_{≥1}M(A) for the space of matrices M(A) = colim_r Ω^∞A^{r×r}, and Proposition 2.9; the T(0)-statement is Waldhausen's.
items.locator: Proposition 3.1 with its proof, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Waldhausen, Algebraic K-theory of spaces, localization and the chromatic filtration, Propositions 1.1, 2.2; Land–Tamme, On the K-theory of pullbacks, Lemma 2.4)

items.name: The Land–Tamme pullback theorem and the ring spectrum A' ⊗~_A B
items.statement: For a pullback square of ring spectra with corners A, B, A', B' there is a ring spectrum A' ⊗~_{A,B'} B, functorial in the square, together with maps from A' and B, such that applying any localizing invariant E to the square with A' ⊗~_{A,B'} B in place of B' gives a pullback square of spectra; moreover fib(A' ⊗~_{A,B'}B → B') ≃ Σ fib(I ⊗_A B → I), where I is the common fibre of the vertical maps and the map is induced by the right B-module structure on I.
items.locator: Used throughout §3, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Land–Tamme, On the K-theory of pullbacks, Ann. of Math. 190 (2019), 877–930, Main Theorem and Remark 1.16)

items.name: Lemma 3.2: connectivity of the multiplication map
items.statement: Lemma 3.2. Let a pullback square of ring spectra with corners A, B, A', B' be given with A connective. If A → A' is n-connective and A → B is m-connective, then the induced map A' ⊗~_{A,B'} B → B' is (m+n+2)-connective.
items.locator: Lemma 3.2, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Localizing invariants truncating on M-acyclic ring spectra
items.statement: For a spectrum M, a localizing invariant E is truncating on M-acyclic ring spectra if for every M-acyclic connective ring spectrum R the map E(R) → E(π_0R) is an equivalence. If a ring spectrum R is M-acyclic then so is τ_{≤k}R for every k, as follows by considering the ring map L_MR → L_M(τ_{≤k}R). Truncating invariants are nilinvariant and satisfy Milnor excision and cdh-descent on discrete rings.
items.locator: §3.2, the paragraph before Lemma 3.3, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. items.name: Postnikov truncations as square-zero extensions
items.statement: For a connective ring spectrum R and k > 0 the map τ_{≤k}R → τ_{≤k−1}R is a square-zero extension, so that there is a pullback square of ring spectra with corners τ_{≤k}R, Hπ_0R, τ_{≤k−1}R and Hπ_0R ⊕ (Hπ_kR)[k+1].
items.locator: Used in the proof of Lemma 3.3, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Lurie, Higher Algebra, 7.4.1.29)

items.name: Lemma 3.3: k-truncating implies truncating
items.statement: Lemma 3.3. Let E be a localizing invariant and suppose that there exists k ≥ 0 such that E(R) → E(τ_{≤k}R) is an equivalence for every M-acyclic connective ring spectrum R. Then E is truncating on M-acyclic ring spectra.
items.locator: Lemma 3.3, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Proposition 3.4: L_{T(n)}K is truncating on L_n^{p,f}-acyclic ring spectra
items.statement: Proposition 3.4. For n ≥ 1, L_{T(n)}K(−) is truncating on L_n^{p,f}-acyclic ring spectra.
items.locator: Proposition 3.4, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary 3.5: the vanishing of L_{T(i)}K(Z/p^n)
items.statement: Corollary 3.5. For every n ≥ 1 and every i ≥ 1, L_{T(i)}K(Z/p^n) = 0. The proof uses that truncating invariants are nilinvariant and Quillen's computation that K(F_p)^∧_p = HZ_p.
items.locator: Corollary 3.5, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Bhatt–Clausen–Mathew; Land–Tamme, Corollary 3.5; Quillen)

items.name: Quillen's computation of the K-theory of a finite field
items.statement: For a finite field with q elements, K_0 = Z, K_{2j} = 0 and K_{2j−1} ≅ Z/(q^j−1) for j ≥ 1; in particular K(F_p)^∧_p ≃ HZ_p and K(F_p) ⊗ Q ≃ Q. The p-complete statement is what makes L_{T(i)}K(F_p) = 0 for i ≥ 1.
items.locator: Used in Corollary 3.5, Remark 4.10 and Example 4.8, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Quillen, On the cohomology and K-theory of the general linear groups over a finite field, Ann. of Math. 96 (1972), 552–586)
items.note: L.1 plans exactly this computation for every finite field, with the Brauer lifting and Adams-operation fibre used in Quillen's proof. The p-completed form K(F_p)^∧_p ≃ HZ_p is the K(1)-local content read off from those groups and is the form the paper uses.

items.name: Group-completion K-theory of an additive ∞-category
items.statement: An additive ∞-category 𝒜 is symmetric monoidal under ⊕, and K^add(𝒜) denotes its group-completion K-theory, a connective spectrum. For a connective ring spectrum R and 𝒜 = Proj^ω(R) the ∞-category of finitely generated projective R-modules, K^add(𝒜) ≃ τ_{≥0}K(R). For X, Y ∈ 𝒜 the mapping space is a grouplike E_∞-space, giving a connective spectrum hom_𝒜(X,Y); when 𝒜 is stable this is the connective cover of Hom_𝒜(X,Y), and Hom_𝒜(X,X) is L_n^{p,f}-acyclic if and only if hom_𝒜(X,X) is.
items.locator: §3.3, the two bullets, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Gepner–Groth–Nikolaus, Universality of multiplicative infinite loop space machines)

items.name: The additive Schwede–Shipley theorem
items.statement: An additive ∞-category generated under finite direct sums and retracts by a single object X is equivalent to Proj^ω(hom_𝒞(X,X)), the ∞-category of finitely generated projective modules over the endomorphism ring spectrum of X. Every additive ∞-category is the filtered colimit of its full subcategories generated in this way by finitely many objects, and K-theory commutes with filtered colimits.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Proposition 3.6, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Proposition 3.6: vanishing of T(i)-local K-theory from acyclic endomorphisms
items.statement: Proposition 3.6. Let 𝒞 be an additive ∞-category such that for each object X the ring spectrum hom_𝒞(X,X) is annihilated by L_n^{p,f}. Then (i) L_{T(i)}K^add(𝒞) = 0 for 1 ≤ i ≤ n, and (ii) L_{T(i)}K(𝒞) = 0 for 1 ≤ i ≤ n if 𝒞 is stable. The proof of (ii) uses the S_•-construction: the equivalence (τ_{≥0}K(𝒞))[1] ≃ |K^add(S_•𝒞)| and the stability of the vanishing hypothesis under passage to Fun(Δ^j,𝒞).
items.locator: Proposition 3.6 with its proof, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: The Thomason–Neeman localization theorem
items.statement: For a compactly generated stable ∞-category and a localizing subcategory generated by compact objects, the sequence of compact objects is an exact sequence of small stable ∞-categories, up to idempotent completion. Applied to L_n^{p,f}, whose acyclics are Ind(𝒞_{>n}) by Lemma 2.6, it gives that 𝒞_{>n} → Perf(S) → Perf(L_n^{p,f}S) is exact.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Lemma 3.7, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Neeman, The connection between the K-theory localization theorem of Thomason, Trobaugh and Yao and the smashing subcategories of Bousfield and Ravenel, Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. 25 (1992), Theorem 2.1)

items.name: Lemma 3.7: the localization sequence for L_n^{p,f}
items.statement: Lemma 3.7. For a ring spectrum A there is an exact sequence of small stable ∞-categories 𝒞_{>n} ⊗ Perf(A) → Perf(A) → Perf(L_n^{p,f}A), and the endomorphism spectrum of every object of 𝒞_{>n} ⊗ Perf(A) is L_n^{p,f}-acyclic. The first category is generated by the A ⊗ F with F a finite p-local L_n^{p,f}-acyclic spectrum, whose endomorphism spectra DF ⊗ F ⊗ A are L_n^{p,f}-acyclic.
items.locator: Lemma 3.7, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Mitchell's theorem: the vanishing of L_{T(i)}K(Z) for i ≥ 2
items.statement: K(Z) — equivalently K(Z[1/p]), and p-adically K(S[1/p]) — vanishes after T(i)-localization for i ≥ 2. This is the height bound that starts the induction in the proof of Theorem 3.8 and in Remark 3.9.
items.locator: Used in the proofs of Theorem 3.8, Remark 3.9 and Proposition 3.12, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Mitchell, The Morava K-theory of algebraic K-theory spectra, K-Theory 3 (1990), 607–626)

items.name: Theorem 3.8: the two halves of purity, in the L_n^{p,f} formulation
items.statement: Theorem 3.8 (reformulation of Theorem A). Let A be a ring spectrum. The map A → L_n^{p,f}A induces an equivalence on L_{T(i)}K(−) for 1 ≤ i ≤ n. If n ≥ 2, the map A → L_{T(1)⊕⋯⊕T(n)}A induces an equivalence on L_{T(n)}K(−). The first part follows from Lemma 3.7 and Proposition 3.6 because K is localizing; the second from the fracture square of Lemma 2.7 with m = 0, the Land–Tamme (or Tamme) pullback theorem, and Mitchell's theorem applied to the bottom row, whose terms are modules over K(S[1/p]).
items.locator: Theorem 3.8 with its proof, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Tamme, Excision in algebraic K-theory revisited; Land–Tamme, Main Theorem)

items.name: Hahn's theorem and its Tate-construction strengthening
items.statement: Hahn: a T(n)-acyclic E_∞-ring (more generally, H_∞-ring) is T(n+1)-acyclic. Clausen–Mathew–Naumann–Noel strengthen this: if R^{tC_p} is T(n)-acyclic then R is T(n+1)-acyclic, for R a commutative algebra in genuine C_p-spectra of the relevant form.
items.locator: Used for the definition of height in §1 and in Remark 3.9, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Hahn, On the Bousfield classes of H_∞-rings, Invent. math.; Clausen–Mathew–Naumann–Noel, Lemma 4.5)

items.name: Kuhn's blueshift theorem
items.statement: For a T(n)-local spectrum X the Tate construction X^{tC_p} vanishes; consequently (L_n^{p,f}S)^{tC_p} is an algebra over L_{n−1}^{p,f}S, which is the blueshift used to run the induction of Remark 3.9.
items.locator: Used in Remark 3.9, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Kuhn, Tate cohomology and periodic localization of polynomial functors, Invent. math. 157 (2004), 345–370)

items.name: The Verdier quotient Fun(BC_p, Perf(R))/Perf(R[C_p]) and R^{tC_p}
items.statement: For a ring spectrum R the Verdier quotient 𝒬 = Fun(BC_p,Perf(R))/Perf(R[C_p]) has End_𝒬(R) ≃ R^{tC_p}, carries a canonical symmetric monoidal structure, and there is a symmetric monoidal functor Perf(R^{tC_p}) → 𝒬; hence K(𝒬) is a module over K(R^{tC_p}).
items.locator: Used in Remark 3.9, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Nikolaus–Scholze, On topological cyclic homology, Acta Math. 221 (2018), Theorems I.3.3(ii), I.3.6 and an analogue of Lemma I.3.8(iii))

items.name: Hesselholt–Nikolaus: the cofibre of the TC assembly map for C_p
items.statement: For a connective ring spectrum R the cofibre of TC(τ_{≥0}R)_{hC_p} → TC(τ_{≥0}R[C_p]) belongs to the localizing subcategory of spectra generated by τ_{≥0}R; in particular it vanishes T(n+1)-locally when R does.
items.locator: Used in Remark 3.9, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Hesselholt–Nikolaus, Topological cyclic homology, Handbook of Homotopy Theory, Theorem 1.4.1)

items.name: Remark 3.9: the Clausen–Mathew–Naumann–Noel vanishing argument
items.statement: Remark 3.9 reproduces the argument for L_{T(n+2)}K(L_n^{p,f}S) = 0 by induction on n. The case n = 0 is Mitchell's theorem. By the Tate strengthening of Hahn's theorem it suffices that K(L_n^{p,f}S)^{tC_p} be T(n+1)-acyclic, and for that that the geometric fixed points of the K-theory of the Borel complete categorical Mackey functor vanish T(n+1)-locally, that is, that both maps in K(L_n^{p,f}S)_{hC_p} → K(L_n^{p,f}S[C_p]) → K(Fun(BC_p,Perf(L_n^{p,f}S))) be T(n+1)-local equivalences. The second uses the Verdier quotient and Kuhn's blueshift with the inductive hypothesis; the first uses Corollary 4.30, which depends only on Theorem 3.8, together with the Hesselholt–Nikolaus theorem.
items.locator: Remark 3.9, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Question 3.10: the Morava K-theory analogue of purity
items.statement: Question 3.10. For a ring spectrum A and n ≥ 2, does the map A → L_{K(n−1)⊕K(n)}A induce an equivalence on K(n)-local K-theory? It would suffice to show that for n ≥ 2 the map A → L_nA induces an equivalence on L_{K(n)}K(−).
items.locator: Question 3.10 and the paragraph after it, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: The identification of stable K-theory with topological Hochschild homology
items.statement: For a connective ring spectrum A and a connective A-bimodule M, colim_r Ω^r fib(K(A ⊕ Σ^rM) → K(A)) ≃ ΩTHH(A;M); for A = S and M a connective spectrum this gives ΩM.
items.locator: Used in Remark 3.11, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy, The local structure of algebraic K-theory, Theorem 5.3.5.1)

items.name: Remark 3.11: the optimality of the Purity Theorem
items.statement: Remark 3.11. For n ≥ 1 the functor A ↦ L_{T(n)}K(A) factors through neither A ↦ L_{T(n)}A nor A ↦ L_{T(n−1)}A. For the first, Hahn–Wilson and Yuan give T(n)-acyclic ring spectra with L_{T(n)}K(A) ≠ 0. For the second, a factorization would make colim_r Ω^r fib(K(S ⊕ Σ^rM) → K(S)) T(n)-acyclic for any connective M that is T(n−1)-acyclic but not T(n)-acyclic, whereas that colimit is ΩM by the identification of stable K-theory with topological Hochschild homology.
items.locator: Remark 3.11, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Hahn–Wilson, Redshift and multiplication for truncated Brown–Peterson spectra; Yuan)

items.name: The stable envelope of an additive ∞-category and nonconnective additive K-theory
items.statement: For an additive ∞-category 𝒞, Stab(𝒞) is the ∞-category of compact objects of Fun^add(𝒞^op,Sp); the fully faithful Yoneda embedding y : 𝒞 → Stab(𝒞), formed with the connective deloopings of the mapping spaces, generates Stab(𝒞) as an idempotent complete stable ∞-category, and τ_{≥0}K(Stab(𝒞)) is the group completion of 𝒞^≃. One therefore sets 𝐊^add(𝒞) = K(Stab(𝒞)); the map K^add(𝒞) → 𝐊^add(𝒞) is a T(i)-equivalence for all i ≥ 1.
items.locator: §3.3, the paragraph before Proposition 3.12, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Hebestreit–Steimle, Hermitian K-theory for stable ∞-categories, Corollary 8.1.3)

items.name: The theorem of the heart and dévissage for abelian categories
items.statement: For a stable ∞-category 𝒟 with a bounded t-structure, K_{≥0}(𝒟) ≃ K_{≥0}(𝒟^♥); in particular K_{≥0}(𝒟) is a module over K(Z), whose T(i)-localizations vanish for i ≥ 2 by Mitchell's theorem. Quillen's dévissage theorem for abelian categories identifies K_{≥0}(𝒜) with K_{≥0}(Mod_{F_p}(𝒜)) when every object of 𝒜 is killed by a power of p.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Proposition 3.12, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Barwick, On exact ∞-categories and the theorem of the heart; Quillen, Higher algebraic K-theory I, Theorem 4)

items.name: Proposition 3.12: Levy's t-structure proof, via a bounded-t-structure fibre
items.statement: Proposition 3.12 (Ishan Levy). For a stable ∞-category 𝒞 there is a fibre sequence K(𝒟) → 𝐊^add(𝒞) → K(𝒞) in which 𝒟 admits a bounded t-structure. Hence K^add(𝒞) → K(𝒞) is (i) a T(i)-local equivalence for i ≥ 2, and (ii) a T(1)-local equivalence if hom_𝒞(X,X)[1/p] = 0 for every object X. Here 𝒟 is the thick subcategory of Stab(𝒞) generated by the cofib(cofib(y(A) → y(B)) → y(C)) for the cofibre sequences A → B → C of 𝒞, which is the kernel of the first-Goodwillie-derivative localization Fun^add(𝒞^op,Sp) → Ind(𝒞), and equals the t-bounded objects of Stab(𝒞).
items.locator: Proposition 3.12 with its proof, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Neeman, Triangulated categories, Ch. 5, and his 2021 work; Pstrągowski–Patchkoria, Theorem 4.26)

items.name: Corollary 4.1: vanishing for T(n)⊕T(n−1)-acyclic ring spectra
items.statement: Corollary 4.1. If R is a ring spectrum which is T(n)⊕T(n−1)-acyclic for some n ≥ 1, then L_{T(n)}K(R) = 0.
items.locator: Corollary 4.1, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary 4.2: the connective cover at heights ≥ 2
items.statement: Corollary 4.2. For n ≥ 2 and any ring spectrum R the canonical map L_{T(n)}K(τ_{≥0}R) → L_{T(n)}K(R) is an equivalence.
items.locator: Corollary 4.2, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary 4.3: redshift vanishing for algebras over an E_∞-ring
items.statement: Corollary 4.3. Let A be an E_∞-ring, B an A-algebra and n ≥ 0. If L_{T(n)}A = 0 then L_{T(n+i)}K(B) = 0 for every integer i ≥ 1.
items.locator: Corollary 4.3, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary 4.4: the connective variant of Theorem A
items.statement: Corollary 4.4. Let A → B be a T(1)⊕⋯⊕T(n)-equivalence between connective ring spectra which induces a surjection on π_0 with nilpotent kernel. Then K(A) → K(B) is again a T(1)⊕⋯⊕T(n)-equivalence.
items.locator: Corollary 4.4, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary 4.5: the same statement for topological cyclic homology
items.statement: Corollary 4.5. Let A → B be a T(1)⊕⋯⊕T(n)-equivalence between connective ring spectra which induces a surjection on π_0 with nilpotent kernel. Then TC(A) → TC(B) is again a T(1)⊕⋯⊕T(n)-equivalence.
items.locator: Corollary 4.5, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: The Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy theorem and the cyclotomic trace
items.statement: For a map of connective ring spectra inducing a surjection with nilpotent kernel on π_0, the square formed by K and TC and the cyclotomic trace is cartesian; this is what transfers Corollary 4.4 to Corollary 4.5 and underlies Corollary E.
items.locator: Used for Corollaries 4.5 and 4.30, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy, The local structure of algebraic K-theory; Clausen–Mathew–Morrow)
items.note: RT.2 plans THH with its circle action and cyclotomic structure and the construction of TC, TC⁻ and TP; RT.3 plans the cyclotomic trace from the same K-theory functor with its naturality and multiplicativity, and names the relative nilpotent comparison theorem — the Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy theorem — as a target with its connective input and p-completion assumptions. No chromatic statement is planned at either stage.

items.name: Remark 4.6: the T(0)-statement
items.statement: Remark 4.6. If A → B is a T(0)-equivalence of connective ring spectra inducing a surjection on π_0 with nilpotent kernel, then K(A) → K(B) is a T(0)-equivalence, and hence so is TC(A) → TC(B).
items.locator: Remark 4.6, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: n-nice and nice morphisms of E_∞-rings
items.statement: A morphism f : R → S of E_∞-rings is n-nice if R and S are connective, f induces an isomorphism on π_0 and after HQ⊕T(1)⊕⋯⊕T(n)-localization, and π_0R ≅ Z; f is nice if it is n-nice for every n ≥ 0.
items.locator: §4.1, the paragraph before Corollary 4.7, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary 4.7: K-theory preserves n-nice morphisms
items.statement: Corollary 4.7. If R → S is an n-nice morphism of E_∞-rings then K(R) → K(S) is again n-nice.
items.locator: Corollary 4.7, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Example 4.8: iterated K-theory of Z/p^k
items.statement: Example 4.8. The canonical truncation map K(Z/p^kZ) → HZ is nice, so that K^{(i)}(Z/p^kZ) → K^{(i−1)}(Z) is an HQ⊕T(1)⊕T(2)⊕⋯-equivalence for every i ≥ 1. The verification uses that K_n(Z/p^kZ) → K_n(F_p) is an isomorphism for n ≤ 0, that K(Z/p^kZ) ⊗ Q ≃ K(F_p) ⊗ Q ≃ Q, and that both K(Z/p^kZ) and HZ are T(i)-acyclic for i ≥ 1, the former by Corollary 4.3.
items.locator: Example 4.8, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Weibel, The K-book, Ch. II, Lemma 2.2 and Ch. IV, Corollary 8.4.1; Weibel, Mayer–Vietoris sequences and module structures on NK_*, Corollary 5.4; Quillen)

items.name: K_0 and the fundamental theorem for quotients by nilpotent ideals
items.statement: For a discrete ring and a nilpotent ideal, K_0 is invariant under the quotient, and by an induction with the fundamental theorem of K-theory the map K_n(R) → K_n(R/I) is an isomorphism for all n ≤ 0.
items.locator: Used in Example 4.8, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Weibel, The K-book, Ch. II, Lemma 2.2 and Ch. IV, Corollary 8.4.1)
items.note: K.3 plans the fundamental theorems for exact categories with dévissage and resolution; K.6 plans Bass's negative K-groups and the fundamental theorem with its Nil terms, which is what the induction into non-positive degrees needs; S.5 plans the fundamental theorem for Laurent polynomial rings. The nilpotent-ideal invariance of K_0 is the degree-zero input and belongs with them.

items.name: Corollary 4.9: the K-theory of Morava K-theory
items.statement: Corollary 4.9. The spectrum K(K(n)) vanishes T(m)-locally for every m ≠ 0, n, n+1.
items.locator: Corollary 4.9, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (compare Angelini-Knoll–Salch for n = 2 and p = 2, 3)

items.name: Dévissage for stable ∞-categories, and the k(m)-K(m) localization sequence
items.statement: Antieau–Gepner–Heller prove a dévissage theorem for nonconnective K-theory of stable ∞-categories, preceded for connective K-theory by Barwick–Lawson; it yields the fibre sequence K(F_p) → K(k(m)) → K(K(m)), where k(m) is the connective cover of K(m) and the first map is restriction of scalars along k(m) → F_p.
items.locator: Used in Remark 4.10 and Remark 4.22, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Antieau–Gepner–Heller, K-theoretic obstructions to bounded t-structures, Proposition 4.4; Barwick–Lawson, Regularity of structured ring spectra and localization in K-theory)

items.name: Remark 4.10: the rationalization of K(K(m))
items.statement: Remark 4.10. K(K(m))[1/p] ≃ K(F_p)[1/p] ⊕ ΣK(F_p)[1/p]. Since K(−)[1/p] is truncating on S[1/p]-acyclic ring spectra, K(k(m)) → K(F_p) is a T(0)-equivalence; the composite K(F_p) → K(k(m)) → K(F_p) is induced by X ↦ X ⊗_{k(m)}F_p, which is id ⊕ Σ^{2p^m−1} by the fibre sequence Σ^{2p^m−2}k(m) →^{v_m} k(m) → HF_p, and therefore zero on any localizing invariant.
items.locator: Remark 4.10, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary 4.11: the K-theory of truncated spheres
items.statement: Corollary 4.11. For any n ≥ 0, L_{T(i)}K(τ_{≤n}S) = 0 for i ≥ 2. Antieau had previously deduced this from a quantitative form of Proposition 3.1 for all n with 4p−4 ≥ n, and conjectured the general statement.
items.locator: Corollary 4.11 with the paragraph after it, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary 4.12: K(BP⟨n⟩) → K(E(n))
items.statement: Corollary 4.12. The map K(BP⟨n⟩) → K(E(n)) is a T(i)-equivalence for i ≥ n+1, and both terms vanish T(i)-locally for i ≥ n+2.
items.locator: Corollary 4.12, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Remark 4.13: Rognes' question on the BP⟨n⟩ localization sequence
items.statement: Remark 4.13. Corollary 4.12 implies that K(BP⟨n−1⟩) → K(BP⟨n⟩) → K(E(n)) becomes a fibre sequence after T(i)-localization for i ≥ n+1. Whether it is a fibre sequence after p-completion was asked by Rognes; the case n = 1 is a theorem of Blumberg–Mandell and the case n = 0 is Quillen's. Antieau–Barthel–Gepner showed that for n ≥ 2 it is not a fibre sequence after rationalization. The chromatic bound for K(BP⟨n⟩) was proved earlier by Angelini-Knoll–Salch when BP⟨n⟩ admits an E_∞-structure.
items.locator: Remark 4.13, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Truncated Brown–Peterson spectra, Johnson–Wilson theories and Morava K-theory
items.statement: BP⟨n⟩ is the truncated Brown–Peterson spectrum with π_* = Z_{(p)}[v_1,…,v_n], E(n) the Johnson–Wilson theory obtained by inverting v_n, k(m) the connective Morava K-theory with π_* = F_p[v_m] and K(m) = k(m)[v_m^{−1}] with π_* = F_p[v_m^{±1}], |v_m| = 2p^m−2; K(0) = HQ. Their basic Bousfield-theoretic properties — L_{T(i)}BP⟨n⟩, the fibre sequence Σ^{2p^m−2}k(m) →^{v_m} k(m) → HF_p and E(n) ≃ L_n^fBP⟨n⟩ — are the input to Corollaries 4.9 and 4.12.
items.locator: §4.2, used in Corollaries 4.9, 4.12 and Remark 4.10, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Waldhausen's A-theory of a space
items.statement: For a connected space X, A(X) = K(S[ΩX]) = K(Σ^∞_+ΩX), so that A(∗) = K(S).
items.locator: §4.2, before Corollary 4.14, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary 4.14: A-theory of a suspension
items.statement: Corollary 4.14. Let n ≥ 1 and let W be a connected space with Σ^∞W T(n)⊕T(n−1)-acyclic. Then the canonical maps A(∗) ⇄ A(ΣW) are mutually inverse T(n)-equivalences. For instance W may be a connected type m complex with m > n. The case n = 0 is due to Waldhausen.
items.locator: Corollary 4.14, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: The Thom spectra y(m)
items.statement: For a fixed prime p there is an essentially unique map of E_2-spaces Ω^2Σ^2S^1 → BGL_1(S^∧_p) sending a generator of π_1 to 1−p ∈ π_1BGL_1(S^∧_p) ≅ Z_p^×, whose Thom spectrum is HF_p by a theorem of Mahowald for p = 2 and Hopkins for odd p. Since Ω^2Σ^2S^1 ≃ Ω(ΩS^3) and ΩS^3 has a cell structure with one cell in every even dimension, one may restrict to the 2m-skeleton F_m(ΩS^3), that is to the James filtration of ΩΣS^2, and the Thom spectra of the maps of E_1-spaces ΩF_{p^m−1}(ΩS^3) → Ω^2S^3 → BGL_1(S^∧_p) are the spectra y(m), with y(0) = S^∧_p and y(∞) = HF_p. The spectra z(m) are the integral versions used at p = 2.
items.locator: §4.2, the setup before Lemma 4.15 and Corollary 4.18, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Mahowald, Ring spectra which are Thom complexes; Antolín-Camarena–Barthel; Mahowald–Ravenel–Shick, §3; Milnor, Corollary 17.4)

items.name: Lemma 4.15: y(m) is L_{m−1}^{p,f}-acyclic
items.statement: Lemma 4.15. The spectrum y(m) is L_{m−1}^{p,f}-acyclic.
items.locator: Lemma 4.15, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary 4.16: the K-theory of y(m)
items.statement: Corollary 4.16. The map K(y(m)) → K(F_p) is an L_{m−1}^{p,f}-equivalence; in particular K(y(m)) vanishes T(n)-locally for 0 < n < m. Remark 4.17 notes that the corresponding statement with T(i) replaced by K(i) follows, and that for p = 2 the latter was studied by Angelini-Knoll–Quigley by trace methods.
items.locator: Corollary 4.16 with Remark 4.17, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary 4.18: the K-theory of z(m)
items.statement: Corollary 4.18. The map K(z(m)) → K(Z_{(2)}) is a T(n)-equivalence for 0 < n < m.
items.locator: Corollary 4.18, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Connective real and complex K-theory and the Bott elements
items.statement: ko and ku are the connective covers of the periodic real and complex topological K-theory spectra KO and KU; β ∈ π_8ko and the Bott class of π_2ku invert to give ko[1/β] ≃ KO and ku[1/β] ≃ KU. For a ko-algebra A, A[1/β] is the corresponding localization.
items.locator: §4.3, Corollary 4.19 and Remark 4.20, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary 4.19: purity for ko-algebras
items.statement: Corollary 4.19. Let A be a ko-algebra. Then the natural map K(A) → K(A[1/β]) is a T(n)-local equivalence for all n ≥ 2.
items.locator: Corollary 4.19, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Remark 4.20: the Blumberg–Mandell localization sequence
items.statement: Remark 4.20. Blumberg–Mandell construct a fibre sequence of connective K-theory spectra K^cn(Z) → K^cn(ku) → K^cn(KU), and likewise for ko and KO, which with Mitchell's theorem gives Corollary 4.19 for A = ko or ku. For ko-algebras A, K(A) is T(n)-acyclic for n ≥ 3 by Corollary 4.1 — shown for A = ku and p ≥ 5 by Ausoni–Rognes and in general by Clausen–Mathew–Naumann–Noel — so Corollary 4.19 has content only at height 2.
items.locator: Remark 4.20, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Blumberg–Mandell, The localization sequence for the algebraic K-theory of topological K-theory, Acta Math. 200 (2008); Ausoni–Rognes)

items.name: Topological modular forms tmf, Tmf and TMF
items.statement: Tmf is the E_∞-ring of global sections of the sheaf 𝒪^top of E_∞-rings on the étale site of the compactified moduli stack M̄_ell of generalized elliptic curves, tmf is its connective cover, and TMF = 𝒪^top(M_ell) is the periodic spectrum obtained over the uncompactified moduli stack, that is by inverting the discriminant Δ. Taking global sections of quasi-coherent 𝒪^top-modules preserves colimits.
items.locator: §4.3, before Corollary 4.21, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Douglas–Francis–Henriques–Hill, Topological modular forms; Behrens; Mathew–Meier)

items.name: Lubin–Tate spectra and Morava stabilizer actions
items.statement: For a formal group 𝔾 of height n over a perfect field k of characteristic p, E_n = E(k,𝔾) is the Lubin–Tate (Morava E-) spectrum, a K(n)-local even periodic E_∞-ring with π_0 the Lubin–Tate deformation ring, carrying an action of the automorphism group of (k,𝔾). It is the target of the chromatic Nullstellensatz and appears in the description of K(1)- and K(2)-local K-theory of tmf.
items.locator: §1 (Redshift) and Corollary 4.21(iv), Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary 4.21: purity for tmf-algebras
items.statement: Corollary 4.21. Let A be a tmf-algebra. (i) K(A) vanishes T(n)-locally for all n ≥ 4. (ii) K(A) → K(A ⊗_{tmf}Tmf) is a T(n)-equivalence for all n ≥ 2. (iii) K(A) → K(A ⊗_{tmf}TMF) is a T(3)-equivalence. (iv) At p = 2 there is a T(3)-local equivalence K(tmf) ≃ K(TMF) ≃ K(E_2)^{hGL_2(F_3)}, with E_2 the Lubin–Tate spectrum of a supersingular elliptic curve over F_4; at p = 3 the analogous statement holds with GL_2(F_3) replaced by the automorphism group over F_3 of a supersingular elliptic curve over F_9. Part (i) was already proved by Clausen–Mathew–Naumann–Noel. The proof of (iii) shows Tmf → TMF is a T(2)-equivalence, because all generalized elliptic curves of height 2 are smooth, so inverting v_2 inverts Δ.
items.locator: Corollary 4.21 with its proof, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Remark 4.22: the Barwick–Lawson localization sequence
items.statement: Remark 4.22. Barwick and Lawson give an analogue of the Blumberg–Mandell localization sequence for certain regular ring spectra, in particular K^cn(Z) → K^cn(tmf) → K^cn(Tmf), which implies Corollary 4.21(ii) for A = tmf and certain other regular tmf-algebras. Antieau–Gepner–Heller extend these sequences to nonconnective K-theory; the difference is irrelevant here, as it vanishes after telescopic localization.
items.locator: Remark 4.22, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary 4.23: K(1)-local K-theory is truncating, and inverting p
items.statement: Corollary 4.23. K(1)-local K-theory is truncating on K(1)-acyclic ring spectra; in fact for a K(1)-acyclic ring spectrum A, L_{K(1)}K(A) = L_{K(1)}K(A[1/p]). This is Corollary C, and uses that K(1)- and T(1)-localization agree.
items.locator: Corollary 4.23, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Corollary 4.24: nilinvariance, Milnor excision and cdh-descent
items.statement: Corollary 4.24. K(1)-local K-theory of discrete rings is nilinvariant and satisfies Milnor excision and cdh-descent. Discrete rings are K(1)-acyclic, and the statement follows from Corollary 4.23 and the general theorems on truncating invariants. For HZ-algebras the last assertion of Corollary 4.30 also appears in Bhatt–Clausen–Mathew, proved by different methods.
items.locator: Corollary 4.24 with the paragraph before it, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Land–Tamme, Theorems 3.3 and A.2; Bhatt–Clausen–Mathew)

items.name: Corollary 4.25: homotopy invariance of K(1)-local K-theory
items.statement: Corollary 4.25. For a connective, K(1)-acyclic ring spectrum A the canonical map L_{K(1)}K(A) → L_{K(1)}K(A[x]) is an equivalence, where A[x] = A ⊗ Σ^∞_+Z_{≥0}. Remark 4.26 adds the smooth affine line: since S{x} → S[x] is a π_0-isomorphism, K(A) → K(A{x}) and K(A{x}) → K(A[x]) are both K(1)-local equivalences, where S{x} is the free E_∞-ring on a degree-0 generator.
items.locator: Corollary 4.25 with Remark 4.26, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043

items.name: Remark 4.27: comparison with Weibel's homotopy K-theory
items.statement: Remark 4.27. For a discrete ring A, Weibel's homotopy K-theory KH(A) is the realization of the simplicial spectrum K(A[Δ^•]) with A[Δ^n] = A[x_0,…,x_n]/(x_0+⋯+x_n−1) ≅ A[x_1,…,x_n]; Corollary 4.25 gives L_{K(1)}K(A) ≃ L_{K(1)}KH(A). Since KH satisfies Milnor excision by Weibel and cdh-descent by Cisinski, this reproves Corollary 4.24.
items.locator: Remark 4.27, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043 (Weibel, Mayer–Vietoris sequences and module structures on NK_*; Cisinski, Descente par éclatements en K-théorie invariante par homotopie)

items.name: Weibel's homotopy K-theory
items.statement: KH(A) is the geometric realization of the simplicial spectrum K(A[Δ^•]); it is homotopy invariant, satisfies Milnor excision and cdh-descent, and agrees with K on regular noetherian rings.
items.locator: Used in Remark 4.27, Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, Purity in chromatically localized algebraic K-theory, read in arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), no. 4, doi:10.1090/jams/1043
items.note: S.5 plans homotopy invariance for regular noetherian schemes and says to define homotopy K-theory by the algebraic-singular construction where it is used, distinguishing it from ordinary K-theory for singular schemes. Milnor excision and cdh-descent for KH are not planned there and are recorded as part of the missing Corollary 4.24 item.

items.name: Remark 4.28: the TC analogue of Corollary 4.23 fails
items.statement: Remark 4.28. The analogue of Corollary 4.23 for topological cyclic homology is false. THH(Z[1/p]) is a Z[1/p]-algebra, so it and hence TC(Z[1/p]) vanish p-adically and a fortiori after T(1)-localization; but L_{T(1)}TC(Z) ≠ 0. For odd p, Bökstedt–Madsen computed the connective cover of TC(Z)^∧_p ≃ TC(Z_p)^∧_p as j ⊕ Σj ⊕ Σ^3ku^∧_p with j the connective cover of the K(1)-local sphere, whence L_{K(1)}TC(Z) ≃ L_{K(1)}S ⊕ ΣL_{K(1)}S ⊕ Σ^3KU^∧_p; for p = 2 Rognes gives a filtration with the same associated graded up to finitely many degrees, and KU^∧_p is rationally nontrivial in infinitely many degrees while the other summands are not.

items.name: Remark 4.29: K(1)-local TC does not commute with filtered colimits of categories
items.statement: Remark 4.29. K(1)-local TC commutes with filtered colimits of rings by Clausen–Mathew–Morrow, but not with filtered colimits of ∞-categories. The filtered colimit colim_k Mod_{Z/p^k}(Perf(Z)) is the ∞-category of p-power torsion perfect Z-modules, giving an exact sequence colim_k Mod_{Z/p^k}(Perf(Z)) → Perf(Z) → Perf(Z[1/p]); commuting with this colimit would force L_{K(1)}TC of the fibre to vanish, since L_{K(1)}TC(Mod_{Z/p^k}(Perf(Z))) is a module over L_{K(1)}TC(Z/p^k), which vanishes because L_{K(1)}K(Z/p^k) = 0. This contradicts Remark 4.28.

items.name: Corollary 4.30: K, the connective cover and TC agree at heights ≥ 2
items.statement: Corollary 4.30. For n ≥ 2 and any ring spectrum A there are natural equivalences L_{T(n)}K(A) = L_{T(n)}K(τ_{≥0}A) = L_{T(n)}TC(τ_{≥0}A). For a T(n)-acyclic ring spectrum with n ≥ 2 this gives L_{T(n)}K(L_{T(n−1)}A) ≃ L_{T(n)}TC(τ_{≥0}A), to be compared with Bhatt–Clausen–Mathew's L_{T(1)}K(A[1/p]) ≃ L_{T(1)}TC(A) for a commutative p-adically complete ring A; no commutativity or completeness at (p,v_1,…,v_{n−1}) is required here.

items.name: Corollary 4.31: group-completion versus Waldhausen K-theory at heights ≥ 2
items.statement: Corollary 4.31. Let 𝒞 be a stable ∞-category and 𝒜 ⊂ 𝒞 an additive subcategory generating 𝒞 as a thick subcategory. Then K^add(𝒜) → K(𝒞) induces an equivalence on T(i)-localization for i ≥ 2. Informally: for T(i)-local phenomena with i ≥ 2 it suffices to group-complete rather than to split all cofibre sequences. Proposition 3.12 gives a second proof.

items.name: Corollary 4.32: sifted colimits
items.statement: Corollary 4.32. For n ≥ 2 the construction A ↦ L_{T(n)}K(A), from ring spectra to T(n)-local spectra, preserves sifted colimits, and likewise on the subcategory of T(n−1)-local ring spectra.

items.name: The orbit category on cyclic subgroups and the assembly map
items.statement: For a group G, 𝒪_𝒞yc(G) is the full subcategory of the orbit category of G spanned by the G-sets G/H with H ⊆ G cyclic; for a ring spectrum A, AG = A ⊗ Σ^∞_+G is the group ring. The assembly map of a functor F is colim_{G/H ∈ 𝒪_𝒞yc(G)} F(AH) → F(AG). The Farrell–Jones conjecture asserts such assembly maps are equivalences for suitable families of subgroups.

items.name: Proposition 4.33: the p-adic TC assembly map for cyclic subgroups
items.statement: Proposition 4.33. For any connective ring spectrum R and any group G the assembly map colim_{G/H ∈ 𝒪_𝒞yc(G)} TC(R[H]) → TC(R[G]) is a p-adic equivalence. It combines a result of Lück–Reich–Rognes–Varisco with the finiteness properties of TC of Clausen–Mathew–Morrow. The assembly map from non-p-completed p-typical TC need not be an equivalence for the family of cyclic subgroups.

items.name: Corollary 4.34: the Farrell–Jones equivalence at heights ≥ 2
items.statement: Corollary 4.34. For any ring spectrum R, any group G and n ≥ 2, the assembly map colim_{G/H ∈ 𝒪_𝒞yc(G)} K(R[H]) → K(R[G]) is a T(n)-equivalence. This is the T(n)-local analogue of the Farrell–Jones conjecture, and was also observed by Marco Varisco for connective ring spectra.
